Como no presente não há «é», diz-se «Я в: Russian has no «am / is / are» in the present tense, so you simply say «Я врач» (literally «I doctor»). Many profession names have no feminine form and are used for both men and women: «Она врач», «Она инженер». Some do have one: студент → студентка, учитель → учительница.

Negar com «не» e dizer de onde você é: Negating with «не» and saying where you are from
Coloque «не» antes da palavra que você n: Put «не» (not) right before the word you are negating: «Я не врач» (I am not a doctor). To say where you are from, use «Я из» + country. The country changes its ending after «из»; for now, learn these as ready-made phrases.

Знакомство / Conhecendo-se: Знакомство / Getting to know each other
Two students meet in a class.
— Oi! Eu sou Lena. Sou estudante. E você: — Hi! I'm Lena. I'm a student. And you?
— Oi, Lena! Eu me chamo Marc. Sou engenh: — Hi, Lena! My name is Marc. I'm an engineer.
— Muito prazer! Você é russo?: — Nice to meet you! Are you Russian?
— No, I'm not Russian. I'm Brazilian.
Para dizer que você NÃO tem algo, use «н: To say you do NOT have something, use «нет», and the noun changes its ending (it goes into the genitive case): «У меня есть сестра» → «У меня нет сестры». Rule of thumb: -а becomes -ы; a final consonant gets -а; after г, к, х, ж, ч, ш, щ you write -и, never -ы. With «нет» you do not use «есть».
I do not have a sister.
He does not have a car.
We do not have a house.
She does not have a dog.
